article_notes: Retrospective analysis of ADVIA 2120 admission data from two prospective Onderstepoort B. rossi cohorts (RLB-PCR confirmed): cohort 1 = 96 infected + 15 controls, Oct 2011-Apr 2013 (ethics V055-11, the Goddard et al. cytokine cohort); cohort 2 = 44 infected + 5 controls, 2014 (ethics V091-13, lymphocyte study, = CB008 cohort). Total 140 infected (15 died, 125 survived) and 20 controls. Overlapping cohort (CH03): cohort 1 shares hospital, period, ethics number V055-11 and the 15 controls with CB145 (97 infected), so most dogs in CB050 are also in CB145 (and cohort 2 in CB008); not independent evidence. Outcome = short-term survival to discharge vs death/euthanasia for poor prognosis during hospitalisation. Outcome groups pooled across both cohorts; per-cohort mortality not given. Not extracted: MPXI-cytokine and MPXI-neutrophil Spearman correlations within the whole infected group, survivors and non-survivors (marker-marker correlations, not marker-severity associations; e.g. MPXI vs IL-6 r = 0.615 in non-survivors only); serum biochemistry and cytokine results that are only in the Supplementary Material (not in the text and previously reported). Exact p values for non-significant outcome comparisons not reported (p_value = NS). Group sizes for MPXI/neutrophil comparisons assumed to be all 140 dogs (Figure 2 gives N = 125 and 15). Skipped: infected vs healthy comparisons for MPXI, segmented and band neutrophils, age and sex.

severity_definitions.label: non-survivors vs survivors
severity_definitions.definition: Short-term outcome: survival until discharge from hospital vs death or euthanasia due to poor prognosis during hospitalisation. Dogs euthanised for other reasons were excluded (cohort 1 criterion). Both cohorts pooled.
severity_definitions.quote: Outcome was noted as short-term survival (i.e., until discharge from hospital), or death/euthanasia due to poor prognosis during hospitalization.

associations.statistic: median (IQR) 22.8 (17.7 – 26.1) vs 19.0 (14.7 – 21.8) (non-survivors vs survivors); Kruskal-Wallis / Mann-Whitney U
associations.quote: MPXI was also significantly higher in the non-survivors (22.8; 17.7 – 26.1) compared to the healthy control dogs (P = 0.011) (Figure 2). There were no significant differences between Babesia-infected dogs that survived (19.0; 14.7 – 21.8) and the healthy control dogs, as well as between the survivors and non-survivors.
associations.location: Results, Comparison of MPXI and Neutrophil Counts, para 1; Figure 2
associations.note: Exact p for survivors vs non-survivors not reported. Non-survivors differed from controls (P = 0.011) but not from survivors.

The ratio of male to female for each group was as follows: healthy control dogs (7:13), survivors (82:43) and non-survivors (10:5), with a significant difference found between groups (P = 0.028).
associations.note: The chi-square P = 0.028 is across all three groups including healthy controls; no survivor vs non-survivor test reported, so not extracted as a severity test. Proportions male are similar.
